title: Machine Learning
description: What machine learning is and its types, linear regression and gradient descent, logistic regression, feature engineering, generalization and model evaluation, and neural networks, with Python practicals.

topics.title: Introduction to Machine Learning
topics.summary: Machine learning is the branch of AI that lets computers learn patterns from data and improve without being explicitly programmed: data and outputs go in and the rules come out. Its main types are supervised, unsupervised, semi-supervised and reinforcement learning, and it raises ethical concerns such as bias and privacy.
subtopics: AI, machine learning, deep learning and generative AI
Traditional programming versus machine learning
Supervised learning: classification and regression
Unsupervised learning: clustering and dimensionality reduction
Semi-supervised and reinforcement learning
Features, labels, instances; parameters and hyperparameters
Applications and ethics; Python tools (Anaconda, pip, scikit-learn)

topics.title: Linear Regression and Gradient Descent
topics.summary: Linear regression fits the straight line (or hyperplane) that best predicts a continuous output, with weights and a bias learned by minimising the mean squared error. Gradient descent finds them by repeatedly stepping against the gradient, with the learning rate setting the step size.
subtopics: Simple and multiple linear regression; y = b0 + b1·x
Estimating b0 and b1 from mean, variance and covariance
Weights, bias, loss and the mean squared error cost
Gradient descent and its update rule
Batch, stochastic and mini-batch gradient descent
Learning rate too small or too large; convergence

topics.title: Logistic Regression
topics.summary: Logistic regression is a supervised algorithm for binary classification that passes a linear combination of features through the sigmoid function to get a probability between 0 and 1, then applies a threshold such as 0.5. It is trained by maximum likelihood, which means minimising the binary cross-entropy loss with gradient descent.
subtopics: What logistic regression is; the click-on-ad example
Assumptions of logistic regression
The sigmoid (logistic) function and the threshold
Odds, log-odds (logit) and the derivation of p(x)
Likelihood, negative log-likelihood and binary cross-entropy
Training with gradient descent

topics.title: Feature Engineering
topics.summary: Feature engineering creates features from raw data or selects the best ones for a model. Discrete data is encoded with one-hot, label or ordinal encoding, and continuous data is transformed with min-max normalisation, log transforms, ratios and rolling windows, before irrelevant features are removed by feature selection.
subtopics: Discrete data: count, categorical, binary, textual
One-hot, label and ordinal encoding
Lexical and semantic text similarity
Exploring continuous data: line, box, heatmap, scatter plots
Min-max normalisation, log transformation, ratios, rolling windows
Feature selection: supervised and unsupervised; filter, wrapper, embedded

topics.title: Generalization and Model Evaluation
topics.summary: A good model generalizes to unseen data, balancing bias (underfitting) against variance (overfitting). Data is split into training, validation and test sets or evaluated with k-fold cross-validation, and models are judged with metrics from the confusion matrix (accuracy, precision, recall, F1) or regression errors (MAE, MSE, RMSE, R²).
subtopics: Bias, variance, underfitting, overfitting and the trade-off
Fixing underfitting and overfitting; regularization, dropout, early stopping
Training, validation and test sets
k-fold and stratified cross-validation
Confusion matrix, accuracy, precision, recall, F1, specificity, ROC and PR curves
Regression metrics: MAE, MSE, RMSE, R²

topics.title: Decision Trees and Random Forests
topics.summary: A decision tree predicts through a sequence of feature tests, choosing splits by entropy, information gain or Gini impurity, and is pruned to avoid overfitting. A random forest combines many trees built on bootstrap samples with random feature subsets, voting or averaging to reduce variance.
subtopics: Nodes, branches and leaves
Splitting: entropy, information gain, Gini impurity, variance reduction
Overfitting and underfitting in trees
Pre-pruning and post-pruning
Bagging and random forests: voting and averaging
Bias–variance in random forests; strengths and weaknesses

topics.title: Neural Networks
topics.summary: An artificial neuron multiplies inputs by weights, adds a bias and passes the sum through an activation function, and a multilayer perceptron stacks input, hidden and output layers of such neurons. The network learns by a forward pass, a loss, backpropagation of gradients with the chain rule, and weight updates by an optimizer.
subtopics: Biological and artificial neurons; the perceptron
Multilayer perceptron: input, hidden and output layers
Activation functions: sigmoid, tanh, ReLU; softmax and linear outputs
Cost functions: MSE, binary and categorical cross-entropy
Forward propagation and backpropagation
Optimizers and hyperparameters
